newsitem.title: UK: CWC and TeleWest talk about common brands - paper.
newsitem.headline: CWC and TeleWest talk about common brands - paper.

text.p: British cable groups Cable and Wireless Communications and Telewest Communications Plc are in talks to form a common television and telephone brand which could lead to a merger, the Times said in its Tuesday edition.
The newspaper said the move would give the firms a powerful weapon in a battle for market share against British Telecommunications Plc and satellite television giant BSkyB.

"TeleWest and CWC are talking about co-operating. We cannot rule out a full merger as a possibility down the road," the Times quoted Fred Vierra, chairman of Denver-based TeleCommunications International, as saying.

TeleCommunications International owns 27 percent of TeleWest while CWC was formed by the 4.5 billion pound ($7.4 billion) merger of Mercury Communications and the Nynex, Bell CableMedia and Videotron cable companies.
The Times said a 5.5 billion pound merger of the two would create one of Europe's largest multi-media groups.

It said Vierra had held preliminary talks with Graham Wallace, chief executive of CWC, about joining forces in some areas, including the branding, promotion and advertising of their telephone and television products.
"What is mandatory is common brands and common promotion, TeleWest has not established a strong brand of our own," the paper quoted Vierra as saying.
A merger would require approval from Britain's Office of Fair Trading and telecoms regulator Oftel, it added.
